storyboard.claim: Predators like Gray read body language to learn a victim's damage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray studying Avery closely, clocking her reaction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the predator's search for the flinch from beat 39.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the watching literal and puts Avery in frame as the one being read.

storyboard.claim: Gray does exactly what was just described.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray alone, watchful.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Confirms the previous beat applies specifically to Gray.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a short confirming beat, sets up the coming contrast with Dr. Smith.

storyboard.claim: Dr. Smith is the clinical psychiatrist meant to be helping her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dr. Smith in his clinical role, addressing Avery.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The promised contrast: Gray's predatory read versus Dr. Smith's clinical one.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts an actual clinician on screen so the contrast has two real bodies, not just an idea.

storyboard.claim: Dr. Smith asks textbook BPD questions off a clipboard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dr. Smith reading questions from his notes while Avery sits across from him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Specifies what the sterile approach actually looks like.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the questions are scripted and read, not felt.

storyboard.claim: His polite structured approach is a language Avery's nervous system does not speak.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery, uneasy, forcing out the words to him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From what he does (textbook questions) to how it lands on her.
storyboard.addedInformation: Centers her discomfort rather than his method.

storyboard.claim: Avery tells him it feels like a business transaction, not human beings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery, pained, calling him out directly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Her own quoted words, finishing the thought from beat 44.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her exact accusation, in her own words.

storyboard.claim: Silence and politeness make Avery incredibly anxious.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery alone, tense in the quiet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the paradox the hosts are about to name.
storyboard.addedInformation: Isolates the exact trigger before the paradox is spelled out.

storyboard.claim: Avery feels more grounded around Lilyale's chaos than in Dr. Smith's calm, flower-filled office.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum weighted toward chaos as where Avery actually feels steady.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the paradox flagged in beat 46.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the counterintuitive weighting visible: chaos, not calm, is where she lands.

storyboard.claim: Chaos matches her internal frequency; a healthy relationship wouldn't register as real.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery standing still amid the facility's noise, unbothered by it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the chaos side of the spectrum reads as safety to her.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reframes chaos from threat to the only register her brain trusts.

storyboard.claim: Her hyperreactive amygdala would reject a healthy dynamic as a trick.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery, guarded, bracing for something to go wrong.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the mechanism behind the previous beat's claim.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows suspicion as her default posture, not an occasional reaction.

storyboard.claim: She needs extreme stimuli just to feel anything besides numb anxiety.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery slumped, flat, unreachable.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the baseline state that only intensity can break through.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the numbness itself, not just the craving for intensity.

storyboard.claim: Gray realizes the key to Avery is neither kindness nor pure cruelty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray holding a key, having worked out how to open her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers what she does respond to, raised in beat 50.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes 'the key' a literal object Gray now possesses.

storyboard.claim: The mechanism is unpredictability, the same logic as a slot machine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A slot machine beside Gray, naming the mechanism before Skinner is introduced.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the answer to the key from beat 51.
storyboard.addedInformation: Bridges to the Skinner explainer with the book's own slot-machine image.

storyboard.claim: Understanding Avery's addiction to Gray requires B.F. Skinner's behavioral psychology.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Skinner box, with Avery reaching toward Gray as the addiction it explains.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the science behind the unpredictability just introduced.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the abstract 'behavioral psychology' claim in the specific box that explains it.

storyboard.claim: Skinner ran operant conditioning experiments using a lever-and-pellet box.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Skinner box itself, with its lever.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the mechanism named a beat earlier.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the actual apparatus the whole analogy rests on.

storyboard.claim: A predictable reward schedule: press the lever, get food every time, the animal learns the association.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from lever press to guaranteed food.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the first, simplest reward schedule before the twist.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the baseline case concrete before it's complicated in the next beats.

storyboard.claim: When the food stops coming entirely, the rat learns the machine is broken and stops trying.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Skinner box, lever untouched now.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The second, opposite case: zero reward extinguishes the behavior.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the case that will contrast with Gray's actual behavior.

storyboard.claim: Skinner's third option, the variable ratio reward schedule, is where it gets dark.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Skinner box again, now for the schedule that actually applies to Gray.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The third case, after all-the-time and none-of-the-time.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the exact schedule the rest of the chapter is built on.

storyboard.claim: With unpredictable reward, the animal presses the lever compulsively.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The lever being hit again and again.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the behavioral result of the schedule just named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes 'compulsively' a repeated physical action, not a mood.

storyboard.claim: Ignoring sleep and every other stimulus, just mashing the button.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The lever, hit without pause.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the compulsion in the plainer, funnier terms the host reaches for.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: mostly restates beat 58, but sharpens it to the host's own summary phrase.

storyboard.claim: The behavior ties to dopamine prediction error in neuroscience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery, thinking it through, as the science is named.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the animal experiment to the brain science behind it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts a human face on the neuroscience term before it's explained.

storyboard.claim: The brain releases dopamine not just on reward, but on anticipating one.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery, caught mid-anticipation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines the prediction-error term just introduced.
storyboard.addedInformation: Separates anticipation from the reward itself, the key distinction for what follows.

storyboard.claim: A 100% predictable reward makes the dopamine spike flatten out over time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery, unmoved, as the predictable case is described.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what happens to anticipation when the puzzle is already solved.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the predictable baseline the unpredictable case will be measured against.

storyboard.claim: When the reward is unpredictable, the brain cannot adapt, and the dopamine spike is massive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery, alert, unable to settle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The unpredictable case, contrasted directly with beat 62.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the failure to adapt as the actual mechanism, not just 'surprise.'

storyboard.claim: The brain becomes hyperfocused trying to crack a pattern that doesn't actually exist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery, straining to find a logic that isn't there.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The payoff of the dopamine explainer: a mind chasing a phantom pattern.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the futility explicit rather than leaving it implied.

storyboard.claim: This is the most addictive behavioral loop in existence, applied to Gray and Avery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray and Avery together, the theory now returning to them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the Skinner detour and returns to the two people it's about.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reconnects the abstract science back to the actual couple.

storyboard.claim: Gray's behavior is intentionally, wildly erratic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray, unreadable, before the two extremes are shown.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the two poles of his behavior described next.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a short setup beat naming the trait before the concrete examples land.

storyboard.claim: One moment he's the epicenter of violence, slamming people against walls, punching bricks until his knuckles bleed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray, mid-violence, against another inmate.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The violent extreme of the erratic behavior just named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the physical cost of the violence, not just the act.

storyboard.claim: He pivots instantly from violence to hyperfocused devotion toward Avery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray turning gentle, attentive to Avery.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tender extreme, immediately after the violent one.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pivot itself, right after beat 67, is the whiplash the chapter is about.

storyboard.claim: He calls her little killer and baby girl and physically tucks her into bed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray tucking Avery in.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A concrete instance of the devotion just named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds 'devotion' in a specific tender, domestic action.

storyboard.claim: Gray tells her there's more on the table to offer than what she knows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gray speaking gently to Avery.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A direct quote continuing the tender scene from beat 69.
storyboard.addedInformation: His exact words, quoted rather than paraphrased.

storyboard.claim: Reading the tenderness right after the threatened murder gives you whiplash.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two rhythms, tenderness and violence, jarring out of sync.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the whiplash between beats 67-70 visible as a single clash.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the mismatch structurally rather than only describing it as a feeling.

storyboard.claim: That whiplash is the trap; consistent cruelty would have let her survival instincts win.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery, caught in the confusion the whiplash creates.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names why the clash just diagrammed is the mechanism, not an accident.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the thesis: the inconsistency itself is the trap, not either extreme alone.

storyboard.claim: If he were consistently cruel, she'd recognize it as a threat and run and hide.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery, poised to flee, the instinct that consistency would trigger.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The counterfactual: what her instincts would do if he weren't erratic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the healthy instinct that unpredictability specifically disables.

storyboard.claim: Because she can never predict which version of him she'll get, her dopamine system locks onto him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Avery reaching toward Gray, unable to stop.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The actual outcome, replacing the run-and-hide counterfactual just shown.
storyboard.addedInformation: Closes the loop: unpredictability produces fixation instead of flight.

storyboard.claim: Picture it like a broken vending machine: put a dollar in, nothing happens.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman viewer facing a vending-machine-style reward device.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Translates the whole Skinner mechanism into an everyday image for the listener.
storyboard.addedInformation: Moves the abstraction from a lab rat to the viewer's own experience.

storyboard.claim: A dollar that always gets a candy bar is nice, but it's just a transaction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman, unmoved by the guaranteed reward.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The predictable version of the vending machine, before the unpredictable twist.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows predictability as boring, setting up the contrast with what's coming.

storyboard.claim: Sometimes the dollar gets a candy bar, sometimes a live hornet stings you in the face.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman recoiling as the machine turns unpredictable and violent.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The twist that turns the predictable machine into the addictive one.
storyboard.addedInformation: The payoff image of the whole vending-machine analogy.

storyboard.claim: You keep pulling the lever; the anticipation alone completely rewires your focus.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman still pulling, unable to stop despite the sting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the compulsion continuing even after the hornet sting just landed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Confirms the obsession outlasts the pain, the point of the whole analogy.

storyboard.claim: The real twist isn't the hornet, it's what happens right after the sting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman, bracing, as the analogy is pushed one step further.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A cliffhanger that withholds the next beat's reveal (Gray handing her the ice pack).
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: sets up the next chunk's reveal without yet showing it.
